pr_title: importccl: support IMPORT in mixed-version cluster
pr_body:
This commit adds support for running IMPORT in a mixed-version cluster.
Note, that it does not add support for running an IMPORT during the
upgrade of a node however. The IMPORT job would need to be restarted in
that case.

Release note (sql change): Add support for running IMPORT in a
mixed-version cluster.
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/57382)

I believe that this also fixes https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/57503.

Will add tests.

Updated with some roachtests that exercise running import in mixed-version clusters and clusters with a decommissioned node.
RFAL

It doesn't look like this needs backporting to versions before 20.2. It looks like https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/release-20.1/pkg/sql/distsql_physical_planner.go#L1064 never populates the NodeAddresses map for unhealthy nodes so https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/release-20.1/pkg/sql/distsql_plan_csv.go#L123 just did the right thing before

issue_context.title: importccl: import fails on clusters with decomissioned nodes
issue_context.body: When performing an import, the import job tries to plan processors on decommissioned nodes and fails with the error `pq: failed to resolve nX: unable to look up descriptor for nX`.
comments:
Hi @pbardea, please add a C-ategory label to your issue. Check out the [label system docs](https://go.crdb.dev/p/issue-labels).

While you're here, please consider adding an A- label to help keep our repository tidy. 

<sub>:owl: Hoot! I am a [Blathers](https://github.com/apps/blathers-crl), a bot for [CockroachDB](https://github.com/cockroachdb). My owner is [otan](https://github.com/otan).</sub>

Adding some more detail here, when IMPORT is given several files to process, it distributes the work across all nodes. Before #57382, it would distribute the work to all nodes in the cluster without checking if they were decommissioned (or otherwise compatible -- e.g. running a different distsql version).

Some possibilities for work-arounds to avoid running into this error:
1. Remove the decommissioned node from the cluster if possible, so that IMPORT does not give it any work

2. Reduce the number of input files specified. This will have the tradeoff of reducing performance of the IMPORT since it will run on fewer nodes. Additionally, since we randomly distribute the work to the nodes there is no guarantee that work will not be scheduled on a decommissioned node, so this might not work every time. If only 1 file is specified, the work should not be distributed -- but only 1 node will be processing the import, which will make it quite slow.

I am aiming to backport the linked fix into all affected versions.

Here is a simple repro using roachprod and a local cluster:

```
# Create a 6 node cluster, but only start 5 of the nodes initially
roachprod create local -n 6
roachprod stage local release v20.2.2
roachprod start local:1-5
roachprod adminurl local:1 --open

# Optionally to make the node dead faster, but not required for the repro
cockroach sql --insecure -e "set cluster setting server.time_until_store_dead = '1m30s'"

# Stop node n5
roachprod stop local:5

# You don't have to wait for the node to be dead to repro. 
# The issue repros if the node is suspect, or dead

# Run an import - conveniently we can use the TPCC workload init command to run an 
# import for us
cockroach workload init tpcc --data-loader IMPORT --drop

# Example error
# I201204 19:01:26.306961 1 ccl/workloadccl/fixture.go:342  starting import of 9 tables
#I201204 19:01:33.364079 25 ccl/workloadccl/fixture.go:472  imported 53 B in warehouse table (1 rows, 0 index entries, took 7.055532s, 0.00 MiB/s)
#Error: importing fixture: importing table order_line: pq: failed to connect to n5 at 127.0.0.1:26265: initial connection heartbeat failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing dial tcp 127.0.0.1:26265: connect: connection refused"

# ------------------
# This is enough to repro. But we can also see that decommissioning the node, 
# and adding another node, does not resolve the problem
#-------------------

# Add a new node to the cluster
roachprod start local:6

# Wait until the cluster rebalances (typically < 60 seconds) then run the import again
cockroach workload init tpcc --data-loader IMPORT --drop

# Example errors:
# I201204 19:02:41.534111 1 ccl/workloadccl/fixture.go:342  starting import of 9 tables
# I201204 19:02:46.264698 118 ccl/workloadccl/fixture.go:472  imported 53 B in warehouse table (1 rows, 0 index entries, took 4.727877s, 0.00 MiB/s)
# Error: importing fixture: importing table order: pq: failed to connect to n5 at 127.0.0.1:26265: initial connection heartbeat failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing dial tcp 127.0.0.1:26265: connect: connection refused"

# Verify node 5 is down but not decommissioned. Then decommission node 5
cockroach node status --insecure
cockroach node decommission 5  --insecure

# Verify node 5 is fully decommissioned
cockroach node status --decommission --insecure

cockroach workload init tpcc --data-loader IMPORT --drop

# Example errors:
# I201204 19:05:23.563527 1 ccl/workloadccl/fixture.go:342  starting import of 9 tables
# Error: importing fixture: importing table order: pq: failed to connect to n5 at 127.0.0.1:26265: initial connection heartbeat failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing dial tcp 127.0.0.1:26265: connect: connection refused"
```

review_comments: not a change for this PR but now I'm sorta wondering why we even SetupAllNodesPlanning if we're not planning on _all_ nodes

we still need SetupAllNodesPlanning here so that the planCtx can learn about the node status of all of the nodes. I think there's an argument to split out `getAllPlannableNodes` out again, which is just a pure function on the `planCtx`. We only need to `getAllPlannableNodes` in import and restore where we round-robin distribute work.

Even in backup, we still need `planCtx` to know about the status of all nodes so it only plans on healthy ones.
